metadata.title: Object (Computer Science) — Comprehensive Knowledge Graph
metadata.description: Connected graph of the computer-science concept of an object: state, behavior, identity, object lifecycle, type and programming paradigms, object relationships, modeling, persistence, distributed systems, security, concurrency, design patterns, and cited source references.
metadata.source_basis: Primarily based on the user-provided Wikipedia article text; broader related concepts are added as clearly described contextual expansions.

entities.name: Object (computer science)
entities.description: An identifiable semantic entity in software with state, behavior, and identity.

entities.name: State
entities.description: The data or condition associated with an object at a particular point in time.

entities.name: Behavior
entities.description: The operations, responses, and effects an object can exhibit.

entities.name: Identity
entities.description: The property that distinguishes an object as an individual entity even when its state resembles another object's state.

entities.name: Attributes
entities.description: Named data characteristics or properties associated with an object.

entities.name: Methods
entities.description: Operations callable on or associated with an object.

entities.name: Object invariants
entities.description: Conditions that should remain true for an object across its valid lifetime or public operations.

entities.name: Object responsibility
entities.description: The role or work an object is assigned within a software design.

entities.name: Object collaboration
entities.description: Interaction among objects whose coordinated behavior provides higher-level functionality.

entities.name: Domain model
entities.description: Representation of concepts, entities, and rules in a problem domain.

entities.name: Real-world entity
entities.description: A person, place, thing, event, or other real-world concept represented by software.

entities.name: Abstract entity
entities.description: A conceptual or invented design entity that does not need a direct physical counterpart.

entities.name: Object reference
entities.description: A language-level value or handle used to access an object indirectly.

entities.name: Pointer
entities.description: A value representing a memory address or location, distinct from higher-level object identity.

entities.name: Memory location
entities.description: A runtime storage location associated with an object representation.

entities.name: Object lifetime
entities.description: The interval during which an object exists and can participate in program behavior.

entities.name: Object creation
entities.description: The process by which an object comes into existence.

entities.name: Object destruction
entities.description: The termination, cleanup, or reclamation phase of an object's lifetime.

entities.name: Object copying
entities.description: Creating another object or representation from an existing object.

entities.name: Shallow copy
entities.description: A copy that duplicates top-level structure while retaining references to nested objects.

entities.name: Deep copy
entities.description: A copy that recursively duplicates nested mutable object structures according to a defined policy.

entities.name: Object equality
entities.description: A rule for determining whether two object references or values count as equal.

entities.name: Reference equality
entities.description: Equality based on whether two references designate the same object.

entities.name: Value equality
entities.description: Equality based on the values or contents represented by objects.

entities.name: Aliasing
entities.description: Multiple references can designate the same object, so changes through one alias may be visible through another.

entities.name: Mutability
entities.description: Whether an object's state can change after construction.

entities.name: Immutability
entities.description: A guarantee or design property that object state cannot change after construction, subject to the definition used.

entities.name: Encapsulation
entities.description: Bundling state and behavior and controlling access to an object's implementation.

entities.name: Information hiding
entities.description: Concealing implementation decisions behind a stable interface.

entities.name: Interface
entities.description: A defined set of operations or capabilities through which a client can use an object.

entities.name: Implementation
entities.description: The internal representation and code that realizes an object's externally visible contract.

entities.name: Class
entities.description: A type or blueprint from which instances may be created in class-based systems.

entities.name: Instance
entities.description: A particular runtime object created from or conforming to a type or class.

entities.name: Class-based programming
entities.description: A model in which classes are central templates for creating objects.

entities.name: Prototype-based programming
entities.description: A model in which objects inherit or delegate behavior through links to other objects used as prototypes.

entities.name: Object-based programming
entities.description: A style providing encapsulated objects, without necessarily requiring inheritance and polymorphism.

entities.name: Object-oriented programming
entities.description: A style commonly characterized by objects, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.

entities.name: Inheritance
entities.description: A mechanism by which a type or object reuses or specializes behavior from a parent type or prototype.

entities.name: Polymorphism
entities.description: The ability to use a common abstraction with different implementations or behaviors.

entities.name: Subtyping
entities.description: A type relationship in which values of a subtype can be used where a supertype is expected, subject to the type system.

entities.name: Dynamic dispatch
entities.description: Selecting an implementation based on the runtime type or receiver.

entities.name: Message passing
entities.description: Sending a request or message to an object to invoke behavior.

entities.name: Method invocation
entities.description: Calling an operation associated with an object or type.

entities.name: Object composition
entities.description: Building a larger object or behavior by combining collaborating component objects.

entities.name: Aggregation
entities.description: A whole-part relationship in which parts can have independent lifetimes, as commonly modeled in UML.

entities.name: Association
entities.description: A relationship in which objects know about or interact with other objects.

entities.name: Delegation
entities.description: Forwarding responsibility from one object to another object.

entities.name: Dependency
entities.description: A relationship in which one component relies on another component's services or contract.

entities.name: Object graph
entities.description: A set of objects and the references or links connecting them.

entities.name: Object network
entities.description: A set of interacting objects across components, processes, or machines.

entities.name: Business object
entities.description: An object representing a business concept, business rule, or business process element.

entities.name: Data Transfer Object (DTO)
entities.description: A data carrier used to transfer information across process or architectural boundaries.

entities.name: Value object
entities.description: A domain model object whose identity is typically defined by its attributes rather than a unique identity.

entities.name: Domain entity
entities.description: A domain object whose identity persists independently of changes to its attributes.

entities.name: Distributed object
entities.description: An object abstraction whose operations or state are accessible across a process or network boundary.

entities.name: Metaobject
entities.description: An object that represents or controls aspects of another object's structure or behavior.

entities.name: Object-capability model
entities.description: A security model in which references to objects convey authority to invoke permitted operations.

entities.name: Database object
entities.description: A database structure or modeled item such as a table, column, view, procedure, or other schema element.

entities.name: Database table
entities.description: A named relational structure containing rows and columns.

entities.name: Database column
entities.description: A named attribute of a relational table.

entities.name: Information system
entities.description: A system whose components, interfaces, and responsibilities can be modeled as objects.

entities.name: Distributed system
entities.description: A system whose components execute across multiple processes or machines.

entities.name: Semantics
entities.description: The meaning of constructs, operations, and relationships in a programming language or model.

entities.name: Programming language
entities.description: A formal language used to express computations and program behavior.

entities.name: Type system
entities.description: Rules that classify values and constrain operations and compatibility.

entities.name: Runtime system
entities.description: Execution machinery that manages objects, calls, storage, and object lifetimes.

entities.name: Garbage collection
entities.description: Automatic reclamation of managed objects that are no longer reachable under a runtime's rules.

entities.name: Resource management
entities.description: Handling object-associated resources such as files, sockets, locks, and handles.

entities.name: Serialization
entities.description: Encoding object data into a transferable or storable representation.

entities.name: Deserialization
entities.description: Reconstructing an object or data structure from an encoded representation.

entities.name: Object-relational mapping (ORM)
entities.description: Mapping between in-memory object models and relational database structures.

entities.name: Unified Modeling Language (UML)
entities.description: A modeling language commonly used to describe classes, objects, associations, composition, and object interactions.

entities.name: Object diagram
entities.description: A UML diagram showing object instances and links at a particular snapshot.

entities.name: Class diagram
entities.description: A UML diagram showing classes, attributes, operations, and relationships.

entities.name: Object-oriented analysis
entities.description: Identifying domain concepts, responsibilities, and relationships as part of analysis.

entities.name: Object-oriented design
entities.description: Designing objects, interfaces, responsibilities, collaborations, and relationships.

entities.name: Object-Oriented Analysis and Design with Applications
entities.description: A well-known book by Grady Booch and collaborators cited in the supplied article.

entities.name: Is Schrödinger's Cat Object-Oriented?
entities.description: Article by Adolfo M. Nemirovsky cited in the supplied source.

entities.name: Distributed Object-Based Programming Systems
entities.description: ACM-catalogued work referenced by the supplied article.

entities.name: Dimensions of Object-Based Language Design
entities.description: Research work referenced by the supplied article.

entities.name: A Brief History of the Object-Oriented Approach
entities.description: Historical overview cited by the supplied article.

entities.name: SQL Demystified
entities.description: Andy Oppel's book cited in relation to database objects.

entities.name: Java
entities.description: Class-based language in which classes ultimately inherit from Object in the conventional Java type model.

entities.name: C#
entities.description: Class-based .NET language in which reference types ultimately derive from System.Object.

entities.name: System.Object / Object
entities.description: Root base type in the standard class hierarchies of Java and C#/.NET.

entities.name: JavaScript
entities.description: Prototype-based language whose objects delegate through prototype chains.

entities.name: Python
entities.description: Multi-paradigm language with class-based object models and runtime object identity.

entities.name: Smalltalk
entities.description: Historically influential object-oriented language.

entities.name: State transition
entities.description: A change from one valid object state to another caused by an operation or event.

entities.name: Constructor
entities.description: An initialization mechanism commonly used to establish an object's initial valid state.

entities.name: Factory
entities.description: A function or object responsible for constructing and sometimes configuring objects.

entities.name: Finalizer / destructor
entities.description: A language/runtime-specific mechanism for cleanup near the end of object lifetime; semantics vary by language.

entities.name: Reference counting
entities.description: A memory-management technique that tracks references to determine when an object can be reclaimed.

entities.name: Ownership
entities.description: A rule or discipline assigning responsibility for an object's lifetime or mutation.

entities.name: Borrowed reference
entities.description: A reference whose use is limited by an ownership or lifetime discipline.

entities.name: Weak reference
entities.description: A reference that does not by itself keep a managed object alive under the relevant runtime's rules.

entities.name: Concurrency
entities.description: Overlapping execution or progress by multiple tasks that may interact with shared objects.

entities.name: Thread safety
entities.description: A property describing whether concurrent access preserves an object's correctness.

entities.name: Synchronization
entities.description: Coordination of concurrent operations to prevent races or establish ordering.

entities.name: Race condition
entities.description: A correctness failure whose outcome depends on timing or interleaving.

entities.name: Object pool
entities.description: A reusable collection of pre-created objects intended to reduce allocation cost or manage scarce resources.

entities.name: Flyweight
entities.description: A pattern that shares intrinsic state among many logical objects to reduce memory use.

entities.name: Proxy
entities.description: An object that controls access to another object or stands in for it.

entities.name: Adapter
entities.description: An object that translates one interface into another expected by a client.

entities.name: Decorator
entities.description: An object that wraps another object to add behavior while preserving an interface.

entities.name: Observer
entities.description: A publish-subscribe relationship in which observers are notified about subject changes.

entities.name: Strategy
entities.description: An interchangeable object encapsulating an algorithm or behavior.

entities.name: Repository
entities.description: An abstraction mediating access to domain objects and persistence.

entities.name: Aggregate
entities.description: A cluster of domain objects governed by an aggregate root and consistency boundary.

entities.name: Aggregate root
entities.description: The designated entry point for modifying an aggregate.

entities.name: Identity map
entities.description: A pattern ensuring a persistence context maintains one in-memory instance per database identity.

entities.name: Unit of Work
entities.description: A pattern tracking changes to objects and coordinating persistence.

entities.name: Capability reference
entities.description: An unforgeable or protected reference whose possession grants specific authority.

entities.name: Least authority
entities.description: Give each component only the authority required for its task.

entities.name: Remote method invocation
entities.description: Invoking object-like operations across a process or network boundary.

entities.name: Network latency
entities.description: Delay affecting remote object calls and distributed collaborations.

entities.name: Partial failure
entities.description: A distributed component can fail while other components remain operational.

entities.name: Consistency
entities.description: Rules governing which states and observations are considered valid across components.

entities.name: Object identity mapping
entities.description: Mapping between runtime identity and a persistent identifier.

entities.name: Primary key
entities.description: A relational key used to identify a row independently of its mutable non-key attributes.

entities.name: Database row
entities.description: A tuple of values in a relational table.

entities.name: Object documentation
entities.description: Descriptions of an object's purpose, invariants, operations, and collaboration contract.

entities.name: Object contract
entities.description: Preconditions, postconditions, and invariants defining correct use of an object.

entities.name: Precondition
entities.description: A condition that must hold before an operation is called.

entities.name: Postcondition
entities.description: A condition guaranteed after an operation completes successfully.

entities.name: Cohesion
entities.description: How strongly an object's responsibilities belong together.

entities.name: Coupling
entities.description: How strongly an object depends on details of other objects.

entities.name: Single-responsibility principle
entities.description: A design principle favoring one coherent reason for a module or class to change.

entities.name: Law of Demeter
entities.description: A principle limiting the breadth of knowledge and navigation among collaborators.

entities.name: Dependency inversion principle
entities.description: A principle favoring dependencies on abstractions rather than concrete implementation details.

entities.name: Encapsulation boundary
entities.description: The boundary across which an object exposes its public contract while hiding internal details.

entities.name: Reachability
entities.description: Whether an object can be reached from roots or other live references according to a runtime's memory model.

entities.name: Identity token
entities.description: A stable identifier used by a runtime or application to distinguish object instances.

entities.name: Object handle
entities.description: An indirect token or reference used to access an object managed elsewhere.

entities.name: Prototype chain
entities.description: A chain of prototype links used by JavaScript property lookup and delegation.

entities.name: Prototype
entities.description: An object used as a delegation target for property lookup and shared behavior.

entities.name: Metaclass
entities.description: A class or type that describes or controls classes/types in systems that expose such a model.

entities.name: Reflection
entities.description: Runtime inspection of object types, members, and metadata.

entities.name: Introspection
entities.description: Inspection of an object's structure or capabilities by a program.

entities.name: Business rule
entities.description: A rule governing valid business state or operations represented by domain objects.

entities.name: Service object
entities.description: An object organizing behavior or operations that do not naturally belong to a single entity.

entities.name: Value semantics
entities.description: Behavior in which values are treated as independent values rather than shared mutable identities.

entities.name: Reference semantics
entities.description: Behavior in which variables/references can designate a shared object identity.

entities.name: Object-capability security
entities.description: Security architecture that uses explicit object references and restricted authority rather than ambient global access.

A programming language defines object constructs and their semantics.
Type systems classify classes and object-compatible values.
